title: Nuclear power plant emergency
tldr: Listen to the official alert for your zone and follow instructions to shelter or evacuate. If told to shelter, go indoors and close windows and doors. Take potassium iodide only if public-health officials direct it; it is not a general radiation antidote.
steps: Use emergency management and plant-area alerts for your actual address.
Move indoors and follow instructions for outside-air ventilation.
Use designated routes and reception centers; do not invent a route through restricted areas.
Use packaged supplies and heed any local contamination restrictions.
next: Keep the local emergency plan, routes and alert channels available before an incident.
watch: Plant emergencies differ from nuclear detonations; a fixed distance or timer is not an all-clear.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Seek zone-specific radiation information by radio or another verified channel. Radiation cannot be measured by smell or sight. Indoors, close openings and reduce outside-air intake while you establish whether your zone must evacuate; do not self-dose potassium iodide or improvise a route through a suspected release.
household: Keep the family together in the correct shelter for the hazard and separate potentially contaminated items from the living area. Use covered food and safe water. Prepare a bag for relocation, but do not send someone outside for it during an active release.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
